ontology_miner_prohibition_enforced_by: rails.probes.pslu_flight.assert_never_calls_ontology_miner (reused verbatim) PLUS rails.probes.pslu_s2_flight._assert_this_module_never_calls_ontology_miner (this module's own source, checked separately -- see that function's own docstring for why the parent's default guard alone cannot scan a different file) -- both checked at rails.probes.pslu_s2_flight import time and again at the top of run_pslu_s2_flight

execution_plan.note: planned_* are ceilings the plan is validated/metered against (contracts.ExecutionPlan); protocol_hash and run_id/attempt_id are assigned by the flying agent's own launcher at flight time, never frozen here. split_identity_hash is IDENTICAL to the parent flight's own value -- this probe reuses the SAME frozen 60-sample manifest, never a fresh draw.

bridge.note: Same bridge convention as the parent pslu-flight.json: every request sends supplied_evidence=[]/evidence_provenance=[] under this same fixed D2 arm -- F1's roster text and A1'r phase 1's closed-set instruction text both live inside a rails 'text' content part FrozenCoreClient never has to translate specially, exactly like the parent's own roster arms.

arm_semantics.F1: format-matched filler control: ONE fixed 100-entry synthetic non-ontology roster (rails.probes.pslu_s2_filler.generate_f1_filler_roster, seed 20260807), rendered byte-identically to A3's own type=value shape via the SAME rails.probes.pslu_flight._roster_packet, identical for every sample (n=60)
arm_semantics.A1r-phase1: closed-set scenario choice over the 18 canonical scenario labels (rails.probes.pslu_s2_flight.canonical_scenario_labels, derived from the frozen roster table's own scenario_rosters keys), deterministically mapped to a canonical label or recorded as an A2-fallback (rails.probes.pslu_s2_flight.map_predicted_scenario_to_canonical) (n=60)
arm_semantics.A1r: self-scoping re-fly, phase 2: the frozen rails.probes.pslu_flight.pslu_supply_packet('A1p', scenario=<A1r-phase1's own parsed label>, rosters=...) roster, scored for official SLU-F1 (n=60, plus 3 silence-swap variants)

phases.phase1: F1's own single-phase request (independent per sample), and A1'r's own closed-set scenario-choice request (independent of F1) -- both fired once per sample
phases.phase2: A1'r's own supply-scored request, keyed on phase 1's own parsed label -- A1'r additionally fires one silence-swapped phase-2 request for each sample named in silence_swap; F1 has no phase 2

silence_swap.selection_rule: sorted(random.Random(f'{seed}:silence-swap').sample(sorted(item['sample_id'] for item in sample_manifest['items']), 3)) -- IDENTICAL rule and seed to the parent flight's own silence_swap block, over the SAME frozen 60-sample manifest, so it reproduces the SAME 3 sample ids (test_pslu_s2_flight_config.py proves this against BOTH this file and the parent's own pslu-flight.json)
silence_swap.note: adds exactly 3 extra requests beyond the base 60+60+60 total, on A1'r's OWN phase-2 request only (never F1, never A1'r's own phase-1 request) -- rails.probes.pslu_s2_flight.run_pslu_s2_flight's own silence_swap_media_relpaths parameter consumes {sample_id: registered_slice_media_relpath} exactly like the parent's own run_pslu_flight

cost_budget.audio_seconds_formula: 182.26s (one full pass over the 60 samples) x 3 sends per sample (F1 + A1'r phase1 + A1'r phase2) + ~9.12s (3 silence-swap extra sends, duration-matched to their own samples) ~= 555.9s

metrics.primary: official SLU-F1 on F1 and A1'r, compared against the CITED consumed A0 (0.1741, docs/checks/speech-aware-evidence-acquisition/2026-08-18-pslu-read/verdict.json, commit d8b71a5) and CITED consumed A3 (0.5961, same source) -- A0 is NOT re-flown by this probe
alongside: phase-1 non-fallback rate / mapping-outcome breakdown / phase-1 scenario accuracy vs gold (scoring-side only)
